messages:
cheng: Heads-up — saw p99 token latency jump from ~220ms to ~1.1s for tenants running on slice-23 in us-west-2 after last consolidation. Pattern: lots of short chat requests, KV cache miss rate spiked. I’m biased toward reverting the consolidation for that slice or carving out very small dedicated slices for SLO-critical tenants. Thoughts?

maria: Do we have per-tenant cache hit and GPU occupancy numbers to quantify impact?

cheng: Yep, dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/abc123/slice-23 — cache hit dropped 94% -> 68%, gpu_util went 60% -> 88% during the 15:00-16:00 PT spike. If we split the slice into a tiny dedicated pool for the top 5 tenants, rough infra delta is ~+0.8% spend for that AZ (~$2.1k/mo).

alex: Two tradeoffs: (1) Carving slices reduces noisy co-tenancy but raises fragmentation + management overhead. (2) We need a routing fallback so lower-tier tenants can be bin-packed elsewhere. Proposal: keep consolidation by default, introduce preemptible "min-slices" for high-SLO tenants + a fast fallback route to a burst pool in same AZ. Also try reducing batch_size for the affected route as a quick latency lever.

sam: We ran a small canary last week reducing batch_size from 32 -> 8 for similar workloads. p95 latency improved ~30% but throughput dropped ~25%. Logs showed more small kernel launches but fewer KV collisions. Pasting the canary snippet below.

```
[2026-03-16T15:12:03Z] canary-runner: route=/chat/compact batch_size=8 p95=210ms p99=480ms throughput=750r/s
[2026-03-16T15:12:03Z] baseline: batch_size=32 p95=320ms p99=1.05s throughput=1000r/s
```

maria: If we go for real-time mitigation, could we add a runtime detector: if KV-miss-rate increases >15% over 5m window, flip affinity to isolate affected tenants and route low-priority traffic to preemptible pool? That would avoid immediate reconfig + let us collect post-trigger metrics.

cheng: Yeah — draft routing config + knob I was thinking:

```yaml
routing_policies:
  - name: high_slo_affinity
    match: tenant.slo == "gold"
    actions:
      - ensure_min_slices: 2
      - fallback_route: burst-pool-usw2
      - runtime_trigger:
          kv_miss_delta_pct: 15
          window_sec: 300
```

alex: Important callout: us-west-2 capacity is tight right now due to a batch of Dedicated reservations. If we physically carve dedicated slices in us-west-2 we may need to pull capacity from us-west-1 or provision extra racks, which introduces cross-region egress or lead time. Cross-region egress at our traffic volumes could blow past that $2.1k/mo — rough estimate: 120 TB/mo * $0.05/GB = ~$6k/mo. Need a precise calc.

maria: Action items: (1) run a targeted rollback of the consolidation for slice-23 in a staging-like env and compare (2) implement runtime KV-miss detector + fallback route (3) cost calc for cross-AZ vs cross-region placement. I'll own (1) and (2), alex owns (3). Sam — can you schedule the rollback in prod-canary and attach logs? tagging @sam

sam: :thumbsup: I’ll schedule the rollback this afternoon into prod-canary and attach canary logs. If rollback helps we can do a quick 24h probe. I’ll also open a PR for the reduced-batch experiments and link it here.

ops-bot: AUTO: created task INFRA-4219 'slice-23 consolidation rollback and KV-miss fallback' assigned to maria, sam, alex. ETA 48h. Link: https://tasks.redwood/INFRA-4219

cheng: Thanks — please paste the canary logs and cost calc in the INFRA-4219 thread so we can close the loop. If rollback doesn't help we will explore the dedicate-min-slice + quota gating approach.
